clue.text: Peer into middle distance?

parts.note: reads as gazing at the horizon, but means a member of the House of Lords who ran middle-distance races

explanation.surface: Someone squints towards the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb of looking; it is a noun, a lord. Sebastian Coe, Olympic 1500m champion, became a life peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sebastian Coe is a former middle-distance runner who was made a baron, so he is literally a peer of that sport.

clue.text: Film a tribute to a former 18 of 15, 16 and 4, 19A and 6?

definitions.text: a tribute to a former 18 of 15, 16 and 4, 19A and 6?
definitions.meaning: the life story of ... Close, captain of Yorkshire, Somerset and England, the setter's hero and a fine batsman

explanation.surface: A movie made in honour of a retired skipper of several cricket teams.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Close, who died in 2015, captained Yorkshire, Somerset and England; the puzzle celebrates him.
explanation.definitionFit: Monty Python's 1979 comedy film has this title, and the same words describe a biography of Brian Close.

clue.text: Weakening fast, Niger struggles to get a grip

indicators.note: the scrambled letters grip, that is enclose, the other piece
the word Niger struggles, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: The West African country, weakening quickly, battles to regain control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed, matching 'Weakening fast'; it is the noun, the Lenten fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Relenting means softening or giving way in one's resolve, close to weakening.

clue.text: Almost stuffy, although smoke-free

parts.note: a close room is airless and stuffy
but means although
with no cigar there is nothing to smoke

explanation.surface: Describes a room that is airless though nobody is smoking.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOSE also names the theme's Brian Close.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an attempt that nearly succeeds but just falls short, meaning nearly.

clue.text: Swollen glands sweep across the nation

indicators.note: the answer sweeps across the boundary between the two words, lying within them

explanation.surface: Swollen glands spread throughout the whole country, like an epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: A sweep is also a cricket shot.
explanation.definitionFit: England is the country, one of the home nations of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Mad farmers seize Noordhoek extremists

indicators.note: the farmers take hold of the extremists, so those letters go inside

parts.note: Boers are Afrikaner farmers, the Afrikaans word for farmer

indicators.note: the extreme letters, first and last, of Noordhoek are taken

explanation.surface: Crazed South African farmers capture militants from Noordhoek, a Cape Town suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonkers is informal British slang for crazy or insane, a direct synonym of mad.

clue.text: Halt playful kiss first

parts.note: a buss is an old word for a smacking kiss
top means first, as in top of the class

explanation.surface: An order to stop the play-fighting and kissing before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halt' looks like an instruction; it is a noun, a stopping place.
explanation.definitionFit: A halt is a minor stopping point on a railway or bus route, a place where vehicles pull up.

clue.text: Matthew bought in curry — he'll likely get the runs

indicators.note: a curry is a mixture of spices, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Matthew ate a takeaway curry and will probably get diarrhoea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the runs' suggests a stomach upset after a curry; in cricket a batsman who is no mug with the bat scores runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone no mug with the bat is a competent batsman, so likely to score runs in cricket.

clue.text: More wide, perhaps

definitions.meaning: in cricket a wide is one example of a run not credited to the batsman

explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, and in cricket wides, byes and no-balls are all extras.

clue.text: Fresh, cooked food's a non-starter for agricultural labourers

indicators.note: food that is cooked is altered, so these letters are reworked
a non-starter loses its start, the opening letter

parts.note: the word food, with 's meaning is

explanation.surface: Fresh home cooking is no good for farm workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a non-starter' drops the first letter of FOOD, leaving OOD, which joins FRESH in the anagram from 'cooked'.
explanation.definitionFit: Serfhood is the condition, collectively the class, of serfs, the bonded peasants who worked the land.

clue.text: Page reported enemy sign

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the words are taken by how they would be heard

parts.note: an enemy is a foe and a sign of the zodiac is Leo, giving foe Leo

explanation.surface: A messenger boy brought news of a hostile signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Page' looks like a person, the messenger; it is a sheet of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a numbered leaf or sheet in a book or manuscript, so it can stand for a page.

clue.text: A few great bats about to be seen at The Oval!

definitions.text: to be seen at The Oval!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the other piece
bats is slang for crazy, so the letters of great are scrambled

parts.note: a few means some

explanation.surface: A handful of fine batsmen will appear at the Oval cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground overlooked by famous Victorian gas holders; 'bats' looks like cricket bats but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian gas holders beside the Oval ground in Kennington are a well-known landmark visible during televised cricket.

clue.text: Cat moves like Tigger without boundaries

indicators.note: the boundaries are the first and last letters, which are dropped

parts.note: Tigger in Winnie-the-Pooh bounces everywhere

explanation.surface: A big cat springs about like the bouncy tiger from Winnie-the-Pooh, unfenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without boundaries' trims BOUNCES to its inner letters; 'boundaries' also nods to cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a wild cat of Central Asian mountains.

clue.text: Slang reflected in gold pub sign

indicators.note: the turned word sits within the other letters

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
PH is the abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: argot is slang or jargon

explanation.surface: A slangy phrase appears mirrored on a gilded pub signboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like part of the pub signboard picture, but it is the definition, a signature.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign something as a fan's keepsake is to give an autograph, the noun-and-verb sense of a signature.

clue.text: Able to pay cash for two ponies with a pound over?

parts.words: two ponies with a pound over
parts.note: a pony is slang for 25 pounds, so two make 50 and one more makes 51, LI in Roman numerals
a quid is a pound in British slang

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone can afford fifty-one pounds, the cost of two racehorses or a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: PONY is British slang for £25 and QUID for £1, so the clue describes 51 quid.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid firm or person has ready cash or assets easily converted, so is solvent and can meet debts.

clue.text: Aware of Tory VIP scandal

indicators.note: a scandal throws things into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone knew about the affair involving a senior Conservative figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Being privy to a secret means sharing knowledge of it, an idiom for being informed.

clue.text: Sidebottom? On the contrary, his team!

definitions.text: Sidebottom? On the contrary, his team!

parts.words: Sidebottom? On the contrary, his team!
parts.note: Ryan Sidebottom played for a county that was no bottom side but top of the table

explanation.surface: A jibe at a cricketer's surname, answered that his club was champion.
explanation.walkthrough: Ryan Sidebottom, a fast bowler, played for this county, which was top, not bottom, of the County Championship in 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire County Cricket Club was Sidebottom's team and won the championship, so it was the side at the top.

clue.text: Beginning of spectacular meteor shower over southern county

indicators.note: only the opening letter of spectacular is used
the scrambled letters are spread over the letter, enclosing it
a shower scatters, so the letters of meteor are scattered

explanation.surface: A dazzling meteor shower is seen across a county in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' rearranges METEOR into OMERET, placed 'over' S. SOMERSET is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is an English county in the West Country, a shire with its own cricket club.

clue.text: Two parts of 3's compound of carbon?

indicators.note: a compound mixes elements, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the last two words of the answer to 3 down are no and cigar

explanation.surface: Chemistry question about two components of a carbon compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like part of the chemistry; it is the anagram signal for the final words of 3 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic chemistry is the study of carbon compounds, so organic means relating to carbon-based substances.

clue.text: He skips and moves about the field

definitions.text: He skips and moves about the field

parts.words: He skips and moves about the field
parts.note: reads as someone hopping across a meadow, but describes the skipper who sets the fielders

explanation.surface: A man skipping and running around a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skips' means acts as skipper; the cricket leader moves fielders about.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket team leader is nicknamed the skipper and directs where the fielders stand.

clue.text: Yo! Mister! He shot Knut's lion!

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A shout at a man who has just gunned down the setter's lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knut's' is the setter speaking of himself; 'lion' means a celebrated person, here Brian Close.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion is a celebrity, someone admired, and from the setter's point of view his own admired idol.

clue.text: Wimp exploits work

parts.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A feeble person takes advantage of a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a feeble, spineless person, an old-fashioned synonym for a weakling.

clue.text: It's found in shell fish served up after pike is gutted

indicators.note: the fish comes after the pike's letters
the inside letters of pike are removed, leaving its outer ones
in a down clue served up means set upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: Seafood dish of shellfish served after a gutted pike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shell fish' tempts a reading as one word, seafood; 'shell' belongs to the definition and 'fish' is TUNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundnut grows inside a papery pod, so it is a kernel found in a shell.

clue.text: European Parliament's a firm friend of the Church

parts.note: EP is the abbreviation for the European Parliament, and the 's stands for is
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: The European Parliament is a staunch ally of organised religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopal describes church government by bishops, so it means relating to the Church.

clue.text: Exists to protect Tory legends

indicators.note: the outer word shields the other one inside it

parts.note: is means exists
Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: Something exists to shield Conservative heroes.
explanation.definitionFit: Legends and icons are both revered figures, celebrated people treated as idols.

clue.text: Speed, pure, Charlie's pushed

indicators.note: Charlie is pushed out of the word

parts.note: chaste means pure or virtuous
Charlie is C in the radio alphabet; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Charlie is being urged to hurry up with something speedy and clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is hurried speed or urgency of movement, a near synonym.

clue.text: It takes spirit; good to get stuck in, go girl!

indicators.note: the letter is wedged between the other pieces

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a shot
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Encouragement to a young woman to be brave and get involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It takes spirit' sounds like courage; it is a small glass that holds a measure of liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: This small tumbler is designed for a single measure of whisky or vodka, a container for spirits.

clue.text: See 1
One on board in international trial

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
a single run is one added to the scoreboard

explanation.surface: A cricketer joins the side for an international match on approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One on board' looks like a passenger or director; in cricket a run is one unit put on the scoreboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A test run is a trial operation carried out before something is used for real.

clue.text: One seeing doctor has to draw in breath

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a pant is a short gasping breath
a tie is a drawn game

explanation.surface: A doctor's visitor is told to take a deep breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw in breath' reads as one action, inhaling; split it, a tie goes inside a gasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone being treated or examined by a medical practitioner is that doctor's patient.
